public_payload.normalized_proposition: If he is right, most GPU data centers will sit inert, likely powered down, and no one will find a use for them.

statement.excerpt: The majority of GPU-based data centers — which really have no other revenue stream — will be left inert, likely powered down, waiting for the day that somebody works it all out, which they won’t,

from_speaker: The majority of GPU-based data centers
waiting for the day that somebody works it all out, which they won’t
our_interpretation: The surrounding paragraph makes this conditional on the predicted OpenAI collapse.
Majority means more than half by facility count, rather than GPU count, electricity capacity or asset value.
The relevant population is GPU-focused data centers operating immediately before the collapse.
Inert means sustained absence of productive workloads or viable replacement customers. Low GPU utilization alone is insufficient.
Powered down is described as likely, so it is not a mandatory condition.
The parenthetical about revenue streams supplies the proposed mechanism; it is not treated as a separate quantified company-money claim.
criteria.support_condition: Following a documented OpenAI collapse, a majority of the defined facilities become unusable for productive commercial work and records establish lasting abandonment without viable alternative uses.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Following the antecedent, decisive records rule out majority abandonment in the defined cohort, or establish viable reuse of facilities claimed to have no possible alternative use. Current utilization alone cannot refute an undated future forecast.
